leadHtml:
CSS CLOCK V0.27.0 BETA

@fzlt/core/css-clock

A page's own CSS @keyframes, on the kernel clock. The look stays in the stylesheet; Fizlet owns the time. Each animation under root is paused and reads its time from one custom property that a timeline moves through the ledger: .led { animation: blink 1s steps(2) infinite paused; animation-delay: var(--fz-t, 0s); } .bug { animation: walk 6s linear infinite paused; animation-delay: calc(var(--fz-t, 0s) - 3s); } - One shared requestAnimationFrame with every other engine on the page; off screen or in a hidden tab it asks for no frames at all. - Settles: after loops plays of span seconds it rests where it started (every animation whose duration divides span is back on its first frame) and the engine sleeps. A pointer over the root, focus inside it or coming back into view plays it again. - Reduced motion: play() lands on the rest frame at once (the still poster). - Recall: destroy() (or aborting signal) gives the root's style back as it was.

CssClockOptions interface BETA

Options for cssClock(): the loop length, how many plays before it rests, the custom property, the frame cap, reduced motion and an abort signal.

export interface CssClockOptions {
    /** Seconds in one play: the loop length (the longest animation, or a common multiple). Default 6. */
    span?: number;
    /** Plays before it rests and the engine settles (default 3). */
    loops?: number;
    /** The custom property the animations read (default "--fz-t"). */
    prop?: string;
    /** Frame-rate cap, e.g. 30 for steps() blinks (default: none, 60 Hz). */
    fps?: number;
    /** Animate (default: yes, unless the visitor prefers reduced motion). */
    motion?: boolean;
    /** Aborting it destroys the clock (Recall included). */
    signal?: AbortSignal;
}
